Barin Ghosh, C.J. (Oral)
 Admittedly tax due has been deposited. Interest
thereon for delay has also admittedly been deposited. For delay in
payment of tax dues, penalty proceedings were initiated.
Revisionist succeeded before the Joint Commissioner of Appeals.
Joint Commissioner of Appeals held that there was good reasons
for the appellant causing the delay. While doing so, Joint
Commissioner of Appeals did not take note of the fact that except
depositing the dues of the Government on time, revisionist
managed its affairs in the manner the same were required to be
managed. The fact remains, revisionist himself extended the credit
line. In consequence, payments due to him were delayed. That
could not be a justification for delaying payment of the
Government dues. The Tribunal, therefore, has correctly held that
the Joint Commissioner of Appeals erred in holding that there was
just reason for delay in depositing the tax dues. The Tribunal,

3
however, has held that the maximum penalty i.e. 50 per cent of the
amount of tax is payable. In doing so, it has not given any just
reason in the orders appealed. Under law, minimum penalty
leviable is 10 per cent of the amount of tax and the maximum
penalty is 50 per cent of the amount of tax. Therefore, in some
cases, the penalty may be 10 per cent and in some cases, the
penalty may be 50 per cent. Why it should be 50 per cent and why
it should not be 10 per cent is required to be justified. That
justification does not appear from the order of the Tribunal. We,
accordingly, remit back all these matters to the Tribunal for
reconsideration of the quantum of penalty to be levied. The
Tribunal must give reasons in respect of each of the defaults and
try to justify levy of penalty in respect thereof.
 2. All the commercial tax revisions stand disposed of.

(Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.) (Barin Ghosh, C.J.)
